dataFlow: When a shopper lands on a sold-out product page, the storefront widget queries live variant availability; if sold out it renders the signup form. On submission the backend records a waitlist entry (idempotent on email + item key) and confirms inline. When inventory is updated, the backend receives the event, resolves the affected variant via an inventoryItem lookup, checks whether stock has crossed from zero to positive, and — if so — opens a new restock run for that item. The notification dispatcher picks up the run, sends emails in signup order up to the available quantity ceiling (respecting quiet hours by queuing delayed jobs), then marks each notified entry as notified and closes the run. When an order is paid, the backend matches line items against recently notified entries within a seven-day attribution window and marks conversions. A product deletion event removes all open waitlist entries and restock runs for that product. The merchant reviews demand, individual subscribers, and conversion stats from the admin dashboard, and configures email templates and quiet hours via settings pages.

triggers.idempotency: if a restock run already exists for this item key in the current restock cycle (same item, available > 0), treat as a no-op until stock returns to zero and rises again
deletion is idempotent; if no waitlist entries or restock runs exist for the product, exit cleanly
if attribution rows already exist for this order external id, treat as a no-op

persistence.name: waitlist_entries
persistence.purpose: Stores every shopper signup for back-in-stock notification at the item level, tracks notification and conversion state, and provides the queue order for fair dispatch.

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: composite natural key shared with restock_runs; encodes product or variant scope, e.g. 'product:123' or 'variant:456'

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: the product this entry belongs to, used for product-deletion cleanup

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: null when the signup is at product level (single default variant); set for variant-level signups

columns.name: unsubscribe_token
columns.purpose: opaque token embedded in email links; used to clear all waitlist entries for this email without requiring login

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle state: waiting, notified, converted, unsubscribed

columns.name: restock_run_id
columns.purpose: the restock run that dispatched the notification to this entry; null until notified

queryPatterns: entries for a given item_key ordered by signed_up_at ascending (queue order for dispatch)
entries with status=waiting for a given item_key to count demand and select the front of queue
all entries for a given email to support global unsubscribe
entries for a given product_external_id to support product-deletion cleanup
entries for a given restock_run_id to support run history drill-in
entries by item_key and status with cursor pagination for admin subscriber list

persistence.name: restock_runs
persistence.purpose: Records each discrete restock event for an item, tracks how many notifications were sent, and enforces the one-notification-per-shopper-per-restock rule.

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: matches item_key on waitlist_entries; scopes the run to a specific product or variant

columns.name: available_quantity_at_trigger
columns.purpose: stock level observed when the restock event fired; used to cap how many shoppers are notified in this run

columns.name: notified_count
columns.purpose: running tally of emails dispatched in this run

queryPatterns: most recent open run for a given item_key to enforce dedup (one active run per item)
all runs for a given item_key ordered by triggered_at descending for admin run history
runs for a given product_external_id for product-deletion cleanup

persistence.name: notification_sends
persistence.purpose: Audit log of every individual email send attempt within a restock run, used for run history display and delivery failure tracking.
queryPatterns: all sends for a given restock_run_id to render run detail in admin
single send by id when recording outcome after email delivery attempt

persistence.name: attribution_events
persistence.purpose: Records a purchase that occurred within the attribution window after a back-in-stock notification, enabling 'lost demand recovered' conversion metrics.

columns.name: waitlist_entry_id
columns.purpose: the notified entry that receives conversion credit

columns.name: order_external_id
columns.purpose: the paid order that triggered attribution

queryPatterns: attribution events for a given item_key to compute conversion rate
attribution events for a given restock_run_id for per-run conversion stats
lookup by order_external_id and item_key for idempotent insert

persistence.name: demand_snapshots
persistence.purpose: Pre-aggregated per-item demand and conversion metrics refreshed after each restock run and each attribution event, enabling instant-load admin dashboard ranking.

columns.name: waiting_count
columns.purpose: current number of entries with status=waiting; primary sort key for the demand ranking

queryPatterns: all rows ordered by waiting_count descending with cursor pagination for admin dashboard ranking
single row by item_key for per-item stats display

persistence.name: email_template_settings
persistence.purpose: Stores the merchant-configured email subject and body template (single-row singleton).

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: singleton row; code enforces at most one row in this table

queryPatterns: fetch the single settings row before every email dispatch

persistence.name: quiet_hours_settings
persistence.purpose: Stores the merchant-configured quiet-hours window that suppresses email dispatch at night (single-row singleton).

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: singleton row; code enforces at most one row in this table

columns.name: start_hour
columns.purpose: 0-23 hour of day when quiet period begins

columns.name: end_hour
columns.purpose: 0-23 hour of day when quiet period ends

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update deliveries for the same restock event — the handler checks for an existing open or dispatching restock run for the item_key before creating a new one and exits as a no-op if one already exists.
Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — attribution insert is keyed on order_external_id + item_key so repeated delivery produces no additional rows.
Duplicate products/delete delivery for the same product — cleanup is idempotent; if no entries remain a second delivery exits cleanly.

Partial restock where fewer units arrive than waiting shoppers — the run caps dispatch at available_quantity_at_trigger; remaining entries stay in waiting status and are picked up by the next restock run.

Notification email delivery failure — the send is recorded as failed with the reason in notification_sends; the waitlist entry is NOT marked as notified so it remains eligible for the next restock run.
Dispatch falls within quiet hours — the send job is rescheduled to fire at the end of the quiet-hours window and the notification_sends row is marked skipped_quiet_hours until the job fires.
A shopper unsubscribes after being notified but before purchasing — their entry transitions to unsubscribed and is excluded from all future runs and the demand snapshot is refreshed immediately.

Stock briefly dips back to zero and immediately rises again while a run is still dispatching — a new run is only opened when no open or dispatching run exists for the item_key, preventing a double-blast within the same restock cycle.
